source_excerpts:
Build native eopkg format 1.2 archives for Nix applications. Original project
code is MIT licensed. Upstream eopkg and its dependencies retain their own
licenses. This backend is package-manager scoped; consumers choose native
providers and distribution metadata.

`makeNativePackage { name; version; payload; dependencies?; configPaths?; ... }`
accepts a producer-prepared filesystem tree. It adds no engine intent or Nix
dependency; ordinary `eopkg` owns and installs its files. Distribution metadata
and native dependency expressions remain consumer policy. The producer supplies
a working target layout; this does not relocate binaries. A native VM executes
a static payload in a target root without `/nix`, upgrades and removes it.

`makeRuntimePackage` accepts `bundledNixStore` and `bundledNixNotices` for a static
ELF client and its upstream notices. Bundling omits the default Nix dependency;
Python and the manager's Python API remain required. Compatible external clients
take precedence, explicit `IMPURIFIER_NIX_STORE` disables fallback, and failed
mutations are never retried through another client. A bundled-client VM repeats
the original lifecycle suite with an incompatible external candidate. The Nix
provider/installer remains deferred.

validation.value:
The emitter validates archives with upstream eopkg's reader. `nix flake check -L`
also boots QEMU and runs the actual pinned eopkg 5.0 client, with native version,
distribution and architecture checks enabled. Coverage includes legacy-runtime
rejection before unpack, dependency solving, offline recovery, flavor switches,
protected and unedited config, batch activation, accounts/services/lifecycle/admin intent,
driver refresh, foreign-root safety, removal and GC. The outer OS/init is NixOS;
preinstalled providers are inventory markers, not installers. The fixture does
not install usysconf and eopkg reports its normal missing-usysconf diagnostic;
full Solus/usysconf integration remains separate coverage.
